messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: Canary error rate spike in eu-west->ap-southeast path. 5xxs up 18% over baseline in last 2m. paging sara oncall.

sara: got the page, joining. anyone on canary rollout?

ryan: I kicked the geo-weight rollout 6m ago — target was 10% eu-west, 90% origin. looks like some hosts in eu are pulling traffic routed to ap-southeast.

mike: observed increased latency and 5xxs from the proxy pool in eu-west. traces show requests bouncing between model-v2 and model-v1. weird.

jon: checking edge routing: the weight table shows eu-west entries OK, but some_hash ring entries point to old origin IPs in ap-southeast due to a partial topology update. possibility: partial BGP session flap + control-plane race.

alice: customers reporting elevated latencies and a few 502s — support queue spiking. tagging accounts with highest impact: AcmeCorp, Finly, Tutorly.

ryan: I just queried the rollout controller: it reports desired weight 10% eu-west, but actual served weight is 33% eu-west -> ap-southeast. also noticing TTL mismatch on edge host records.

mike: logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] proxy-eu-03 -> upstream ap-southeast-01 model-v1 502 Bad Gateway
[2026-03-15T10:12:06Z] proxy-eu-03 -> upstream eu-west-02 model-v2 200 OK (slow)
```

jon: running quick `dig` from control plane shows some edge nodes returning legacy A records with 60s TTL while controller pushed 300s — likely partial DNS cache flush.

sara: we need to stop the rollout and flip kill-switch. ryan can you abort the rollout now? also notify on-call infra to look at BGP adjacency.

ryan: aborting rollout... calling deploy-bot: `/rollout abort geo-split/2026-03-15-10`

deploy-bot: ack — rollout abort initiated. Starting automated fallback to stable pool. Progress: 0% -> 5% -> 18% (rolling back in batches).

mike: put feature flag `geo-weight-split` to `off` for all regions. `cfgtool set feature.geo-weight-split false --env prod`

(sara reacts with :thumbsup:)

jon: infra team seeing BGP session flaps between eu-agg-1 and peer-asn 64520 around 10:05Z. working on steadying sessions, will post when fixed.

alice: support: notifying top impacted customers with status update. message drafted: "We're investigating intermittent 5xx/latency in EU; we've paused rollout and initiated rollback; we'll follow up within 30m."

mike: after abort commands, errors dropped to 3% in 40s, latency back to baseline for most requests. still some stragglers hitting ap-southeast.

ryan: pushing a targeted cache invalidation to edge nodes: `edgectl flush --selector region=eu-west --type a-record`

jon: cache invalidations acked on 7/9 eu-edge nodes. two nodes were unreachable due to mgmt-plane TLS issue; working to restore.

incident-bot: note — on-call handoff scheduled in 45m. sara, will you keep as primary until handoff?

sara: yes staying on. mike you'll be secondary. jon keep me posted on BGP.

mike: monitoring dashboards: rate and latency graphs flattening. no new customer complaints for last 10m.

alice: summary for postmortem: rollout controller and control-plane cache inconsistency + partial BGP adj flaps allowed stale DNS responses -> cross-region traffic drift -> mixed model versions and elevated 5xxs. mitigation: abort rollout, flip feature flag, edge cache invalidation, infra restored BGP sessions.

ryan: will file a rollout safety ticket: add pre-rollout consistency check to verify DNS TTL parity and BGP adjacency health. also throttle batch size if any region has >5% cache mismatch.

jon: I'll attach BGP logs and edgectl outputs to the incident.

sara: good. assign follow-ups: (1) ryan - safety check for rollout controller, (2) jon - harden mgmt-plane TLS to ensure edge visibility, (3) mike - add alert for served-weight drift >5%. set sev2->P0 if customer error rate >10%.

alice: I'll send the external follow-up in 20m once we have artifacts. good work team. closing immediate page, keeping incident channel open for PM/ops. :white_check_mark:
